display.purpose: Public question-first moments and unusually important learner decisions.

body.purpose: Operating copy, source explanations, and recovery guidance.

label.purpose: Sparse source, position, version, and authority metadata.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Feedback when a source candidate changes review state.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single dominant action in a bounded work surface.
components.css: .ds-primary { min-height: 52px; border: 1px solid #111714; border-radius: 6px; background: #111714; color: #fffdf8; padding: 14px 18px; font: 700 16px/1.2 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-primary:hover { background: #185e62; border-color: #185e62; } .ds-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #185e62; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Source Status
components.description: Plain semantic state that does not resemble a button.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: #7b561a; font: 750 11px/1.3 SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace; letter-spacing: .08em; } .ds-status i { width: 8px; height: 8px; background: currentColor; transform: rotate(45deg); }

narrative.overview: A calm working surface where questions, connected sources, learner actions, and evidence can be inspected without decoration impersonating certainty.
keyCharacteristics: One dominant question or action per viewport
Source and authority states in plain language
Purposeful motion only for state change

rules.name: The Authority Color Rule
rules.body: Accent color communicates who or what owns a state. It is never a decorative category label.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Routine containers use one structural signal and no ambient card shadow.

dos: Show coverage, freshness, and authority where the student makes a decision.
Preserve unknown, stale, conflicting, unavailable, and not-tested states.
donts: Do not open on a card-grid dashboard, chatbot, grade forecast, or mastery percentage.
Do not turn learner confirmation into institutional truth.
